teams.heading: Jake White eyes trusted Springbok ally for Fiji coaching team
teams.body: Jake White is reported to be eyeing a trusted Springbok ally to join his Fiji coaching staff, but the appointment is not confirmed in coverage so far. The hire would be the next piece of a set-up White is building before the November Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy. Fiji's assistant picks remain the open question.

teams.heading: Benhard Janse van Rensburg stood down from rugby indefinitely after two concussions
teams.body: Borthwick has confirmed Benhard Janse van Rensburg will play no part in the autumn campaign, after a specialist advised a number of weeks away from contact rugby. The Bristol centre, who made his Test debut against Fiji in July, was knocked unconscious tackling England team-mate Henry Pollock in Bristol's defeat to Northampton. He misses the Australia, Japan and New Zealand Tests and finals weekend, and his next chance could come in the Six Nations.

lead.why: A new injury story that takes a centre out of England's autumn squad for all three Nations Championship matches, and it is not the Fin Smith story already covered.

teams.heading: Jeremy Ward's France eligibility still awaits World Rugby special permission
teams.body: Jeremy Ward remains in limbo over whether he can play for France at all. The 30-year-old is in the 42-man squad but will train without featuring against Fiji, the Springboks or Argentina, and his eligibility depends on World Rugby granting special permission. He will only complete his five-year residency in 2027, and his four Junior Springboks appearances at the 2016 U20 Championship tie him to South Africa, which was then designated their second national team. No World Rugby decision has been reported.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell opts against replacing Garry Ringrose in Ireland's November squad
teams.body: Andy Farrell has decided against calling up any replacement for Garry Ringrose, despite uncertainty over Tadhg Furlong's availability, the IRFU said on Tuesday. Furlong, 33, is due before a disciplinary committee after being cited for an alleged groin grab against Munster. Jimmy O'Brien is following return-to-play protocols after a concussion, and Sam Prendergast continues rehab from a wrist injury.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item that is not a repeat of the Ringrose withdrawal, and it turns on Ireland's own selection decision.

teams.heading: Italy host reigning world champions South Africa at Turin's Allianz Stadium
teams.body: Italy's first home fixture in the Nations Championship is the opener against reigning world champions South Africa, played at Juventus' Allianz Stadium in Turin. The stadium was presented in September and marks the third consecutive year it has hosted international rugby. Quesada's side then face Argentina in Genoa and Fiji in Udine before the finals at Twickenham.

lead.why: It is the only Italy-owned item in the pack not already covered in previous editions, and it sets up the opening Nations Championship Test.

teams.heading: Ollie Leatherbarrow earns first Scotland call-up in 37-man Nations Championship squad
teams.body: Newcastle back-rower Ollie Leatherbarrow has been called up by Scotland for the first time, and the English-born 24-year-old is the only uncapped player in Gregor Townsend's 37-man squad for the Nations Championship. He qualifies through his grandmother from Perth and has 11 Scotland U20 caps, according to Planet Rugby. Townsend's group also brings back Huw Jones, who missed the July tour through injury, while Grant Gilchrist, recently back from injury, is a notable absentee.

lead.why: It is a Scotland squad story about a new cap, while the NEW Townsend item repeats today's already-run belief story and the Fagerson item has no usable facts in the pack.

teams.heading: BBC analysis: 76 of Wales' past 100 debutants born in Wales
teams.body: The BBC has traced the past 100 men to make their Wales debuts, and the pathway is less Welsh than the badge suggests. Of the 100, 76 were born in Wales, 17 in England and seven elsewhere, but 78 learned their rugby up to age 16 in Wales, with Cardiff's catchment supplying 30. Dewi Lake, Adam Beard and Jac Morgan now play outside Wales, while Louis Rees-Zammit and Dafydd Jenkins made the journey across the border.

lead.why: It is a fresh BBC analysis of how Wales players are developed, and it avoids the Page and Dyer call-up already covered and the pundit piece.

teams.heading: Matías Moroni placed on standby as Santiago Chocobares awaits HIA outcome
teams.body: Matías Moroni is on standby for the Ireland Test after Santiago Chocobares was left waiting on the outcome of a head injury assessment following a knock for Toulouse. Moroni is on 99 caps, so a call-up would give him the chance to reach 100, though he has not played for the Pumas since a facial injury against Australia in August. Chocobares, capped 31 times, is the player whose status decides it.

lead.why: The Chocobares HIA and Moroni's chance of a 100th cap is a fresh angle that is distinct from the three-changes story already reported today.

teams.heading: Ewen McKenzie predicts Mark Nawaqanitawase will end up in Wallabies jersey
teams.body: Former Wallabies coach Ewen McKenzie has predicted Mark Nawaqanitawase will end up playing for Les Kiss' side, though the back three star has yet to choose between Australia, Fiji and Italy. The 26-year-old, who has 11 Wallabies caps with the last in 2023, has signed with the Saitama Wild Knights in Japan, and McKenzie wants more clarity first: "I'm probably looking for him to make some clear statements, just to tidy a few things up." Ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup, that decision matters.

lead.why: A new story about a Wallabies-eligible star's Test future, with a former Wallabies coach going on record about it.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie says All Blacks defence has made good shifts recently
teams.body: Rennie says the All Blacks are improving on defence as the season wears on. "I think defensively we've made good shifts in the last few weeks," he said after naming the squad for the northern leg, pointing to Tana Umaga's work on defence alongside Mike Blair's attacking gains. Rennie says the side had just 10 days of preparation before the July opener against France. With four tough Tests still to come, he believes time has been good for them.

lead.why: Rennie's on-record assessment of the defensive improvement is a fresh angle on the squad news, not a rehash of the injury and return stories already covered.

teams.heading: Handré Pollard faces scans as André Esterhuizen is sent home for assessment
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus is sweating on two key men. Bulls fly-half Handré Pollard was substituted in the 34-26 win over Ulster with a hamstring injury and is set for scans, with no timeframe on a return. Utility flanker/centre André Esterhuizen came off 52 seconds into the Sharks' win over Cardiff with an ankle issue and has been sent back to South Africa for further assessment. Pollard could also be a doubt for the Boks further down the track, and Esterhuizen has featured in seven Tests this year.

lead.why: It is a new injury story about two current Springboks, Pollard and Esterhuizen, ahead of the Nations Championship, and it is distinct from the Kolbe news already covered.
